messages:
alex: heads-up — saw a perf regression on the canary cluster after the recent kernel-routing tweak. p50 for chat+RAG flows up ~35ms. I traced it to kernel selection flipping when prefix cache hitrate drops below ~10%.
maria: cc @sam @dasha — which model/quant config? can you paste repro steps?
sam: saw a similar spike on prod1 yesterday, p95 went through roof. reproducer: long conversation prefix (~2500 tokens) + RAG documents appended -> lots of unique prefixes -> cache miss storm.
alex: details: model=redwood-opt-13B-q4, runtime flags: continuous_batching=on, batch_coalesce=adaptive. Observed behavior: fallback to unfused attention kernel for small coalesced micro-batches which increases per-token latency.
dasha: interesting — I think the kernel heuristic prefers the narrow-gemm fallback when coalesced batch size < 4. With high prefix-cardinality the coalescing is poor and kernel chosen is suboptimal.
sam: profiling snippet from canary logs:
```
canary-node-3: prefix_key_cardinality=18342
kv_cache_hits=198 (3.7%) kv_cache_misses=5136 (96.3%)
kernel_selected=attn_unfused_v1
avg_coalesced_batch=2.1
p50_token_ms=12.4 (baseline 8.7)
```
alex: quick experiment: forced kernel selection -> fused_attn_v3 on same canary. p50 token latency dropped from 12.4 -> 7.9ms but GPU mem rose ~8% (temp buffers). Cost per-token increased slightly.
maria: could this be a cache key explosion? we recently started storing `session_meta` json inside the prefix key in the legacy shim — that would increase cardinality massively.
sam: confirmed — many keys differ only by ephemeral `client_session_id` or order of metadata fields. example key samples: `prefix_v2|user:123|meta:{"a":1,"b":2}` vs `prefix_v2|user:123|meta:{"b":2,"a":1}` -> different hash.
dasha: proposal: canonicalize prefix key -> drop ephemeral fields (client_session_id, last_active_ts) and canonicalize JSON ordering. canonical_key = sha256(prompt_text + user_id + model + sorted_static_meta).
alex: warmup strategy idea: synthetic prime of top-2k common conversation prefixes on boot (like embeddings warmers). plus adaptive prefetch for RAG: if request contains >N docs, prefetch KV shards for those doc prefixes.
prod-oncall: rolling canary applied with prefix canonicalization patch (alex/sam) — infra-bot reports deploy status below.
infra-bot: deploy started: canary-group-2026-03-18T08:12Z
infra-bot: deploy finished: canary-group-2026-03-18T08:18Z — success
prod-oncall: early telemetry: miss rate dropped from ~18% -> ~5% on patched canaries. p50 improved accordingly. :thumbsup:
maria: observed side-effect: fused kernel increases peak GPU memory due to extra temp buffers. we need a kernel routing policy: prefer fused when miss_rate > X and free_mem > Y, else use memory-slim kernel.
sam: also add telemetry: histogram metric for `prefix_key_cardinality` per-route and per-minute, and gauge for `kv_cache_hit_rate` with 1m/5m windows. these will help auto-trigger prefetch or kernel preference.
dasha: assign follow-ups: (1) alex -> perf PR with canonicalization + telemetry + short-term warmup script, (2) sam -> add kernel routing policy flags + mem checks, (3) maria -> validate cost delta for fused kernel on billing env. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to finalize.
alex: I'll open the PR and include the profiling output + canary comparison and a small synthetic warmup generator. tagging @prod-oncall for rollback plan if mem pressure appears.
prod-oncall: noted — rollback playbook prepared. ping once canary has been at 1h stable.
alex: thanks all. next steps tracked in the perf ticket (#INF-8421).
